name: Filter cHPI
summary: Removes continuous head-position-indicator (cHPI) and optionally power-line noise from raw MEG data with MNE-Python mne.chpi.filter_chpi, with before/after PSD plots and an HTML report.
description: Uses MNE's iterative-fitting cHPI filter, recommended over notch filtering because cHPI signals are modulated by head movement, to remove the coil frequencies (and line noise when include_line is true) from the MEG sensors. Use it on recordings acquired with cHPI coils active, before further preprocessing. Without cHPI information the App stops unless allow_line_only is set, in which case only line noise is removed.

inputs.description: Raw MEG data in MNE FIF format recorded with cHPI coils active.
inputs.requirements: Must contain cHPI information unless allow_line_only is true.

outputs.description: Raw MEG data with cHPI (and line) noise removed (raw.fif).
Power spectral density plots before and after filtering.
HTML report comparing original and filtered data.

parameters.description: If true, also filter line (powerline) noise, in addition to cHPI.
Time step to use for cHPI amplitude estimation, in seconds.
Time window to use to estimate the amplitudes, in seconds, or "auto" for MNE's automatic window selection.
The external order for SSS-like interference suppression; the SSS bases are used as projection vectors during fitting.
If true, allow filtering line noise only, even when no real cHPI information is present.

citations.text: Hayashi S., Caron B. A., Heinsfeld A. S. et al. brainlife.io: a decentralized and open-source cloud platform to support neuroscience research. Nature Methods 21, 809-813 (2024).
Gramfort A. et al. MEG and EEG data analysis with MNE-Python. Frontiers in Neuroscience 7:267 (2013).
